newsitem.title: ITALY: Man missing, feared dead, after rains hit Italy.
newsitem.headline: Man missing, feared dead, after rains hit Italy.

text.p: A man was swept away in his car by a raging torrent and feared dead on Wednesday after torrential rains battered northern Italy, civil authorities said.

They said police on a bridge had seen the man, a 48-year-old electricity worker, swept off in his small car shortly after midnight when the Vermenagna river at Roccavione in the Piedmont region of northwest Italy burst its banks.
The car was found five km (three miles) from the scene but there was no trace of the body.

Heavy rains on Tuesday caused several rivers in northern Italy to break their banks, flooding roads and forcing the evacuation of dozens of people from their homes. Southern Italy has also been affected.
About 200 residents from a small community near the town of Cuneo in the Piedmont region were cut off when the bridge connecting the village to the main road was washed away, rescue services said.
Firefighters also evacuated 30 patients from a private clinic in the town of Robilante as well as several families after a stream there broke its banks.
The same area was devastated by severe floods in 1994 which killed more than 60 people.
Further flooding occurred on Wednesday near Bologna in north-central Italy, where some 150 residents from the village of San Giovanni in Persiceto had to be evacuated.
Weather forecasters have predicted that the torrential rain which has lashed Italy for the past two days should now ease.
